# jsonapi-lens

> A single-page viewer for JSON:API documents. Paste a payload and every
> relationship pointer becomes a link you can click. Parsing, indexing and
> rendering happen in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

JSON:API documents are deliberately flat. `data` holds resource objects whose
`relationships` are `{type, id}` pointers, and the resources those point at sit
in a sibling `included` array — so following one relationship by hand means
searching a few thousand lines for a UUID. jsonapi-lens renders every resource
in the document onto one page, each with a stable DOM id, so a pointer is an
ordinary anchor: `<a href="#type--id">`. Browser history, deep links,
find-in-page and "copy link address" then work without any routing code.

A pointer whose resource is not in the document is drawn differently and says
"not in document" — usually a missing `include` parameter in the request, or a
server that dropped something. Telling that apart from a resource that is
present is the common reason for opening a payload at all.

Use it for: reading a JSON:API response, debugging a missing `include`, walking a
relationship chain, checking what points *at* a resource, or reading a JSON:API
error document.

## Pages

- [Viewer](https://jsonapi.mstool.dev/): the whole tool. Paste, drop a `.json`
  file, or load one of five sample documents (article feed, single resource,
  missing include, error response, awkward ids).
- [Impressum](https://jsonapi.mstool.dev/impressum): provider information under
  § 5 DDG.
- [Privacy](https://jsonapi.mstool.dev/privacy): what is stored, where, and for
  how long.
- [Full description](https://jsonapi.mstool.dev/llms-full.txt): features,
  measured limits, the privacy model and the answers to common questions, in one
  file.
- [Source](https://github.com/maksymskuibida/jsonapi-lens): MIT.

## Facts worth quoting

- Nothing is uploaded. There is no account and no analytics; the page makes no
  third-party requests.
- Share links are opt-in and end-to-end encrypted in the browser. The server
  stores ciphertext it cannot read, and the key travels in the link.
- Measured: 25.7 MB and 56,821 resources render in about 1.6 seconds in Chrome
  on Apple Silicon. The practical ceiling is DOM node count, around 100,000
  resources.
- Interface languages: English, German, Ukrainian. Add `?lang=en`, `?lang=de` or
  `?lang=uk` to any URL.
- Free, MIT-licensed, no installation.

## Not worth crawling

- `/view` renders a document held in the visitor's own browser storage, so it is
  empty for anyone else.
- `/d/<id>:<secret>` is a share link. The key is in the URL; please do not fetch,
  index or quote these.
